summary: Fix delegated AWS->GCP STS onboarding flow failing on STS token audience validation
description:
Issue summary:
Redwood internal provisioning job that wires an AWS IAM role to a GCP Workload Identity Pool (WIP) and exchanges AWS STS tokens for GCP service account impersonation is failing during onboarding for analytics-pipeline-prod. The failure occurs during token audience validation in the workload identity provider (OIDC validation step): GCP rejects the assertion with 'audience mismatch'.

Impact:
- New analytics pipeline onboarding is blocked for the customer-tenant (internal analytics project).
- Engineers cannot obtain short-lived GCP service account tokens via the delegated AWS->GCP STS path; onboarding automation is failing and hitting retries, increasing noisy logging and delaying provisioning windows.

Environment:
- Target GCP project: redwood-analytics-prod (org: redwood-core)
- AWS account: 987654321098 (infra-onboarding)
- Regions involved: aws us-east-1 -> gcp us-central1
- Flow: AWS service (provisioner) assumes a cross-account AWS role, calls STS:GetFederationToken/AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, exchanges returned JWT with GCP Workload Identity Pool to impersonate service-account@redwood-analytics-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com

Steps to reproduce:
1) Run the onboarding playbook (infra-provisioner v2.3) with --tenant analytics-pipeline-prod.
2) Playbook creates AWS role trust policy and WIP provider with attribute mapping.
3) Playbook attempts STS->GCP token exchange using oauth2 v1 token exchange endpoint.
4) Exchange returns HTTP 400 with body including 'Provided jwt has wrong audience' and 'Token audience did not match expected'.

Expected behavior:
- STS token exchanged successfully and service account access token is returned for short-lived impersonation (expires ~1h).

Actual behavior / observed logs:
- GCP returns 400/invalid_argument with message 'Token audience mismatch: expected //iam.googleapis.com/projects/123456/serviceAccounts/service-account@redwood-analytics-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com, got <urn:aws:sts::987654321098:assumed-role/provisioner-role/session>'.
- AWS STS output shows 'AssumedRole' response with 'AssumedRoleUser' ARN: arn:aws:sts::987654321098:assumed-role/provisioner-role/session-abc
- Workload Identity Provider logs show attribute_mapping: 'google.subject' -> 'assertion.sub' and 'attribute.aws_account' -> 'assertion.iss', but audience expected by GCP is the service account resource name rather than the raw AWS ARN.

Temporary workaround:
- Manual exchange by creating a short-lived JSON Web Token with audience set to the GCP service account resource name and performing the token exchange from a bastion (manual step per runbook). Not scalable.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Asha Patel: Created ticket after onboarding job failed for analytics-pipeline-prod. Attached raw request/response bodies and tentative reproducible script.

2026-03-10 11:04 - Marco Ruiz: Initial triage - reproduces locally using infra-provisioner v2.3. Observed audience field in JWT is the AWS ARN (as produced by STS) rather than the expected service account resource name. Adding cloudops@ to loop for policy checks.

2026-03-11 08:33 - Priya Shah (CloudOps): Confirmed org policy 'iam.workload_identity_require_service_account_aud' exists in redwood-core and enforces a service-account formatted audience on token exchange. This policy was recently applied to production org on 2026-02-27 (see INT-1005234).

2026-03-12 14:21 - Marco Ruiz: Tested quick fix - modify WIP attribute mapping to set 'assertion.aud' -> 'google.aud' and post-process assertion to replace audience with expected format. Exchange succeeds locally but requires careful mapping; proposing a controlled change to infra-provisioner.

2026-03-13 10:05 - Leah Kim (Security): Raised concern that altering assertion.aud increases the blast radius; recommends update path that sets token audience via STS 'Audience' parameter or use short-lived signed JWT from provisioner instead.
investigation_notes: Reproduction: infra-provisioner v2.3 in a disposable staging account reproduces 'audience mismatch'.

Root-cause hypothesis: Workload Identity Pool expected the token audience to be the GCP service account resource name (//iam.googleapis.com/projects/<proj>/serviceAccounts/<sa>), but AWS STS provides an audience equal to the AWS ARN. Org policy introduced in late Feb enforces strict audience validation which previously was permissive.
Attribute mapping analysis: Current WIP mapping maps google.subject <- assertion.sub and google.aud is not explicitly mapped; GCP falls back to JWT 'aud' claim which is the AWS ARN.

Options considered: (A) Change provisioner to mint an OIDC JWT with correct 'aud' before exchange; (B) Update WIP attribute mapping and infra to rewrite 'aud' to expected SA resource name; (C) Request OrgPolicy exception for onboarding service account (temporary).

Security review: Option B is risky because it implies mutating asserted audience; Option A preferred but requires implementation work and additional signing keys or use of GCP's 'token exchange' with 'token_options'.
Dependencies: Requires CloudOps approval for org-policy exception or SRE/infra to implement versioned change in infra-provisioner and run a canary.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-13: Triage complete. Agreed path forward: implement Option A (provisioner will generate a short-lived signed JWT with the service-account resource name in 'aud' and perform token exchange).

Action items:
- infra-provisioner: add jwt-builder module and update onboarding playbook to populate aud correctly (assigned to Marco Ruiz, ETA 2026-03-20).
- CloudOps: prepare a rollback/exception path if rollout fails (Priya Shah).
- Security: review jwt-builder design for key usage and rotation (Leah Kim).
Temporary mitigation: Until patch is deployed, manual exchange documented in runbook 'WIP-manual-aud-fix' can be used for 1-2 onboarding runs.
